Architecture¶

Architectural pattern¶

The application uses Django’s Model-Template-View (MTV) architecture, Django’s version of an MVC-style pattern. Models define relational data and domain state. Views coordinate requests, permissions, forms, and workflow operations. Templates render HTML responses. URL configurations connect incoming paths to views. Django forms validate input, and accounts.services contains reusable booking-expiry logic.

Component responsibilities¶

Component

Project responsibility

accounts.models

User, guide, availability, booking, review, and administrator-decision data.

accounts.forms

Input parsing, validation, normalization, and form widgets.

accounts.views

HTTP request handling, access checks, workflows, and response selection.

accounts.services

Reusable business operation for expiring requests.

accounts.urls

Named account routes for registration, booking, guide management, and reviews.

templates/

Shared layout and feature-specific HTML pages.

config/settings.py

Django apps, middleware, templates, authentication, database, email, and static/media configuration.

Request lifecycle¶

Browser
  -> Django URL resolver
  -> View (authentication, authorization, workflow)
  -> Form validation
  -> ORM models / reusable service
  -> SQLite by default, or configured MySQL
  -> View
  -> Django template or redirect
  -> Browser

The Django middleware stack provides sessions, authentication, messages, localization, CSRF protection, and common HTTP handling. HTML is rendered on the server using Django templates, Bootstrap, and the project’s CSS.

Why MTV fits this project¶

The project is composed of relational workflows: email verification, guide approval, date availability, booking requests, trip completion, and reviews. Django’s ORM and forms represent these workflows directly, and server-rendered templates keep the current interface in one application without a separate frontend API. This structure also makes each concern easier to locate as features change.
